Jordan / Laura —

I reviewed the test matrix Nora attached and sketched a pragmatic validation checklist that maps to our runtime capabilities. I’m attaching the BridgeKit compatibility checklist (MD) — it includes the following recommended gates:

1) Environment sanity: correct image tags, served endpoints reachable from Redwood sandbox, TLS certs present.
2) Auth flows: token-based adapter auth, refresh behavior, error handling for 401/429.
3) Functional: end-to-end request/response for streaming and non-streaming flows; sample payloads included.
4) Performance: synthetic load test simulating 5 concurrent clients with 5 req/s each; capture 95th p95 token latency and end-to-end p50.
5) KV/cache behavior: verify adapter preserves KV cache/population where applicable so we don’t double-cache.
6) Observability: logs include request_id, model_id and include structured error codes (see checklist).

Notes:
- For perf baselines, BridgeKit should aim for end-to-end p50 < 400ms and p95 token latency < 1s for 8k context small-ops; these are conservative and can be adjusted after initial run.
- If they use GPU-backed inference for their adapter, we need to confirm supported quantization; I’ll coordinate with infra if we see unusual kernel failures.

I’ll join the call Thursday and bring a short runbook for how we’ll run the sandbox acceptance tests.

Sergio Alvarez
Senior Partner Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: BridgeKit certification pathway & sandbox acceptance

Thanks Jordan / Sergio — following up after our internal run: we completed the smoke items but hit two recurring failures in the streaming path when Redwood’s runtime sends chunked tokens at high QPS.

Failure summary:
- Case #1: intermittent 502 from adapter when concurrent streams > 8; reproduction steps and logs attached (see bridgekit-test-matrix.csv row 12).
- Case #2: token ordering occasionally mismatched for long sessions (>3k tokens) when both streaming and KV cache are enabled.

We attached the test matrix with per-case logs and a short replay script to reproduce. We believe both issues are addressable on our side (race in buffer flush, and a missing sequence-check for merged chunks). We’ll prioritize a fix but wanted Redwood to be aware as it affects the acceptance schedule.

Also: can you confirm whether Redwood expects adapter responses to include a final delimiter byte in the streaming protocol (we currently do not emit an explicit delimiter).

Thanks — Nora (on behalf of QA)

Appreciate the fast follow and the detailed repro — very helpful.

Short summary and next steps:
- Acknowledge issues: we’ve read the attached rows and logs. The streaming 502 and ordering mismatch are blockers for certification but not showstoppers.
- Action owners: BridgeKit QA to push a patched adapter build (target Thu EOD) — Samir and Nora.
- Redwood validation: Sergio to run a focused streaming stress test once patched (we’ll use the same replay script).
- Timeline: target re-run Friday 17 Jul; if green we’ll proceed to acceptance and finalize the certification MOA.

Operational notes:
- Streaming delimiter: Redwood runtime can accept a final delimiter but does not require it; however ordering must be preserved across chunk boundaries. See note in checklist (bridgekit-compat-checklist.md).
- DocuSign: I’ll share the draft MOA and a short DocuSign link for signature once we have a green run.
- Jira: created PARTNER-394 to track the streaming fixes and test re-run.

Jordan Blake
